"He won't be worth a cuss. Look--those hands never did a lick of work--but he will fill the list," he added, walking about nervously and sizing me up with apparent approbation.

I mentioned the idea to some of my friends: the first burst out laughing at the end of my opening sentence, so I refrained from entering into further details. The second said there were a hundred books about Cats already.

arxiv-1604-03640.title: Bridging the Gaps Between Residual Learning, Recurrent Neural Networks and Visual Cortex Written in 2016, released as it is.
arxiv-1604-03640.creator: Qianli Liao, Tomaso Poggio
arxiv-1604-03640.description: Abstract We discuss relations between Residual Networks (ResNet), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) and the primate visual cortex. We begin with the observation that a special type of shallow RNN is exactly equivalent to a very deep ResNet with weight sharing among the layers.

arxiv-1708-07612.title: Cooperative “folding transition” in the sequence space facilitates function-driven evolution of protein families Journal: arXiv
arxiv-1708-07612.creator: Akira R. Kinjo
arxiv-1708-07612.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Akira R. Kinjo. In the protein sequence space, natural proteins form clusters of families which are characterized by their unique native folds whereas the great majority of random polypeptides are neither clustered nor foldable to unique structures. Since a given polypeptide can be either foldable or unfoldable, a kind of “folding transition” is expected at the boundary of a protein family in the sequence space.

arxiv-2301-06493.title: Mapping quantum geometry and quantum phase transitions to real space by a fidelity marker
arxiv-2301-06493.creator: Matheus S. M. de Sousa, Antonio L. Cruz, Wei Chen
arxiv-2301-06493.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Matheus S. M. de Sousa, Antonio L. Cruz, Wei Chen. The quantum geometry in the momentum space of semiconductors and insulators, described by the quantum metric of the valence band Bloch state, has been an intriguing issue owing to its connection to various material properties. Because the Brillouin zone is periodic, the integration of quantum metric over momentum space represents an average distance between neighboring Bloch states, of which we call the fidelity number.

arxiv-2407-14792.title: FedPartWhole: Federated domain generalization via consistent part-whole hierarchies
arxiv-2407-14792.creator: Ahmed Radwan, Mohamed S. Shehata
arxiv-2407-14792.description: Abstract Federated Domain Generalization (FedDG), aims to tackle the challenge of generalizing to unseen domains at test time while catering to the data privacy constraints that prevent centralized data storage from different domains originating at various clients. Existing approaches can be broadly categorized into four groups: domain alignment, data manipulation, learning strategies, and optimization of model aggregation weights.

arxiv-2410-14455.title: Quadratic torsion orders on Jacobian varieties
arxiv-2410-14455.creator: Mohammad Sadek, Hamide Suluyer
arxiv-2410-14455.description: Abstract . We establish the existence of hyperelliptic curves of genus g ≥ 2 g\geq 2 defined over ℚ \mathbb{Q} whose Jacobians possess rational torsion points of order N N where N = 4 ​ g 2 + 2 ​ g − 2 N=4g^{2}+2g-2 or 4 ​ g 2 + 2 ​ g − 4 4g^{2}+2g-4 .

arxiv-2503-10919.title: Data-Driven Soft Robot Control via Adiabatic Spectral Submanifolds
arxiv-2503-10919.creator: Roshan S. Kaundinya \affilnum 1, John Irvin Alora \affilnum 2, Jonas G. Matt \affilnum 3, Luis A. Pabon \affilnum 2, Marco Pavone \affilnum 2 and George Haller \affilnum 1
arxiv-2503-10919.description: Abstract The mechanical complexity of soft robots creates significant challenges for their model-based control. Specifically, linear data-driven models have struggled to control soft robots on complex, spatially extended paths that explore regions with significant nonlinear behavior. To account for these nonlinearities, we develop here a model-predictive control strategy based on the recent theory of adiabatic spectral submanifolds (aSSMs).

arxiv-2504-14897.title: Physics-Aware Compression of Plasma Distribution Functions with GPU-Accelerated Gaussian Mixture Models
arxiv-2504-14897.creator: Andong Hu, Luca Pennati, Ivy Peng, Stefano Markidis
arxiv-2504-14897.description: Abstract Data compression is a critical technology for large-scale plasma simulations. Storing complete particle information requires Terabyte-scale data storage, and analysis requires ad-hoc scalable post-processing tools. We propose a physics-aware in-situ compression method using Gaussian Mixture Models (GMMs) to approximate electron and ion velocity distribution functions with a number of Gaussian components.

plos-pone-0002194.description: PLOS ONE research article. Susceptibility or resistance to infection with Cryptosporidium parvum ( C.parvum ) correlates with Selenium (Se) deficiency in response to infection. pmc-11311059.title: Field Application of an Innovative Approach to Assess Honeybee Health and Nutritional Status
pmc-11311059.creator: Cecilia Rudelli, Roberta Galuppi, Riccardo Cabbri, Thomas Dalmonte, Luca Fontanesi, Giulia Andreani, Gloria Isani, Juan José Pascual
pmc-11311059.description: Simple SummaryHoneybees are vital pollinators, essential for maintaining ecosystems and biodiversity, but there is rising concern about the health of managed honey bee colonies, especially in heavily human-influenced ecosystems. Multiple factors contribute to this decline, including environmental conditions, forage quality, and pesticide use.

pmc-11385278.title: Developing a predictive nomogram for mortality in patients with extrapulmonary acute respiratory distress syndrome: the prognostic value of serum soluble thrombomodulin, lung ultrasound score, and lactate
pmc-11385278.creator: Yang Yang, Yue Wang, Guoguo Zhu, Siya Xu, Jie Liu, Zhongzhi Tang
pmc-11385278.description: Objective: This study aimed to elucidate the prognostic significance of serum soluble thrombomodulin (sTM), lung ultrasound score (LUS), and lactate levels in patients with extrapulmonary acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), with the goal of refining mortality risk prediction in this cohort.

pmc-11483336.title: Comparison of surgical margins and adjuvant therapy for head and neck cancer by hospital type
pmc-11483336.creator: Douglas R Farquhar, Nicholas R Lenze, Jason Tasoulas, Siddharth Sheth, Jose P Zevallos, Catherine Lumley, Jeffrey Blumberg, Samip Patel, Trevor Hackman, Mark C Weissler, Wendell G Yarbrough, Andrew F Olshan, Adam M Zanation
pmc-11483336.description: BackgroundDifferences in patient populations and outcomes by hospital type are becoming increasingly relevant as health care systems shift to value-based care models. There is a paucity of literature on patient-level and hospital-level differences for patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC).

pmc-11566873.title: Laparoscopic resection of a spontaneous gastrocutaneous fistula in an adult – A case report
pmc-11566873.creator: Andrew F. Sabour, Hannah Murawsky, Brian Ward
pmc-11566873.description: IntroductionPersistent gastrocutaneous fistula (GCF) remains a rare but known complication after gastrostomy tube removal. In children, the gold standard of treatment is surgical through an open fistula takedown. Adults, on the other hand, have a much smaller incidence rate, creating a more difficult dilemma in management.

pmc-11708291.title: Endoluminal Wound Vacuum Therapy: A Paradigm Shift in Managing Esophageal Bronchial Fistula
pmc-11708291.creator: Liam Cato, Ray Chihara, Min P. Kim
pmc-11708291.description: Esophageal bronchial fistula after Ivor Lewis esophagectomy is a challenging complication. Surgical treatment is definitive, but it carries high morbidity and mortality, whereas esophageal stents have been shown to be temporary measures. We highlight the case of a patient who was treated with endoluminal wound vacuum therapy. The fistula healed after 9 days of therapy.

pmc-12470016.title: Cannabis sativa Root Extract Exerts Anti-Nociceptive and Anti-Inflammatory Effects via Endocannabinoid Pathway Modulation In Vivo and In Vitro
pmc-12470016.creator: Seo-Yul Jang, Hye-Lin Jin, Ga-Ram Yu, Dong-Woo Lim, Won-Hwan Park, Dana Maria Copolovici
pmc-12470016.description: Cannabis sativa root has traditionally been used to relieve pain and inflammation, but its pharmacological properties remain underexplored due to low levels of psychoactive cannabinoids. This study aimed to investigate the anti-inflammatory and antinociceptive effects of the ethyl acetate fraction of Cannabis sativa root (CSREA) using in vivo rodent pain models.

pmc-12588355.title: Single site of water-resistant asymmetric Bi–Ov–Mn for robust VOC ozonation at ambient temperature
pmc-12588355.creator: Yuqin Lu, Huayang Zhang, Hua Deng, Jianguo Ding, Tingting Pan, Wenjie Tian, Yunbo Yu, Changbin Zhang, Wenpo Shan, Shaobin Wang, Hong He, Joseph S. Francisco
pmc-12588355.description: Manipulating the geometries and electronic structures of oxygen vacancies (Ovs) in oxides to increase their catalytic activity has been a critical focus of research, but the processes remain challenging, particularly because of the significant interference caused by ubiquitous water vapour.

pmc-12654089.title: Identifying Aortic Arch Branching Variations Using Advanced Imaging Techniques
pmc-12654089.creator: Elisabeth M Mandler, Moritz Horodecki-Tuchslau, Johannes M Mittendorfer, Franz Kainberger, Lena Hirtler, Yi-Jen Chen
pmc-12654089.description: Background and Objectives: The branching pattern of the aortic arch (AA) is highly variable, with the typical supra-aortic branching configuration observed in about three out of four cases. Even though some variants carry a heightened risk for certain diseases and intraoperative complications, they are often underrepresented in standard textbooks.

pmc-12752219.title: Diagnosis and surgical management of an acquired cervical tracheoesophageal fistula in a Shih Tzu following foreign body removal
pmc-12752219.creator: Hannelore De porte, Bart Van Goethem
pmc-12752219.description: BackgroundEsophagorespiratory fistulae are rare pathological communications between the esophagus and the respiratory tract. While acquired bronchoesophageal fistulae have been sporadically documented in dogs, tracheoesophageal fistulae, particularly in the cervical region, are exceptionally rare. This case report is the first to describe an acquired cervical tracheoesophageal fistula in a dog following esophageal foreign body retention.

pmc-13084696.title: Hematology in times of crisis: Lessons learned and strategic priorities from the EHA–ASH Joint Workshop on Ukraine
pmc-13084696.creator: Oleksandr Istomin, Taisiya Yakimkova, Reggie Belkhedim, Natacha Bolaños, Konstanze Döhner, Arnold Ganser, Torsten Haferlach, André Ilbawi, Arman Kacharian, Roman Kizyma, Sergiy Klymenko, Sybiryna Korenkova, Frank Leebeek, Oleksandr Lysytsia, Bohdan Medvediev, Wojciech Mlynarski, Dietger Niederwieser
pmc-13084696.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). okun, Mats Heyman, Charlotte Niemeyer, Alexandra Müller Published: 2026 Armed conflict poses profound and sustained challenges to the delivery of hematological care, particularly for patients requiring complex diagnostics, multimodal therapies, and long‐term follow‐up. Children and adults with hematological malignancies and nonmalignant blood disorders are among the most vulnerable populations in humanitarian emergencies, as their care depends on uninterrupted access to specialized diagnostics, blood products, pharmacotherapy, cellular therapies, and highly trained multidisciplinary teams.

pmc-13296965.title: Azithromycin Mitigates Experimental Cryptosporidiosis-Driven Ileocecal Adenocarcinoma by Modulating Autophagy, Apoptosis, and PI3K/AKT Signaling
pmc-13296965.creator: Walaa H. El-Maadawy, Eman S. El-Wakil, Marwa Hassan, Gamal A. Abo Sheishaa, Noha F. Zahran, Mohammed S. El Faramawy, Mohammed H. Abdallah, Eman A. Elsayed
pmc-13296965.description: Background/Objectives: Cryptosporidium parvum (C. parvum), a waterborne intestinal parasite, causes severe, persistent infections in immunocompromised hosts and has been linked to the onset of ileocecal adenocarcinoma. However, the molecular pathways linking chronic infection to carcinogenesis remain unclear. Nitazoxanide (NTZ), the only FDA-approved drug for this infection, shows limited efficacy.

pmc-13336568.creator: Da Kang, Song‐Zuo Xie, Yong‐Zhou Luo, Xin‐Pei Deng, Xi‐Rong Tan, Ze‐Geng Chen, Ling‐Xing Zeng, Gong Chen, Pei‐Rong Ding, Zhi‐Zhong Pan, Rong‐Xin Zhang

pmc-13350142.title: First proctological application of a noncontact nitrous oxide cryotherapy device treating nonmalignant intra- and perianal HPV-related lesions
pmc-13350142.creator: H Ruymbeke, J Geldof, T Holvoet, M Surmont, D De Looze
pmc-13350142.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and aimAnal human papillomavirus (HPV) infection can cause benign and precancerous intra- and perianal lesions. Multiple treatments, including liquid nitrogen cryotherapy, are available with varying efficacy, safety and logistic issues. Little consensus exists considering best clinical practice.

pmc-13365160.title: Case 24: A 42-Year-Old Woman With Fever and Shock

pmc-13485790.title: Changes in saliva composition during different training phases in professional football players
pmc-13485790.creator: Antoon J. M. Ligtenberg, Ektor C. Petras, Kamran Nazmi, Henny Solleveld, Marja L. Laine, Sergio Bizzarro
pmc-13485790.description: ObjectiveThis study investigated changes in salivary biomarkers collected by oral rinsing during different phases of a standard professional football training, and how these changes correlated with perceived training intensity.MethodsThis study included 28 professional football players. Saliva was collected by means of oral rinse with water.

pmc-13651234.title: Comparative analysis of the complete multi-chromosomal mitogenome of an antitussive herb Fritillaria unibracteata
pmc-13651234.creator: Song Lu
pmc-13651234.description: BackgroundA renowned antitussive herb, Fritillaria unibracteata P. K. Hsiao & K. C. Hsia, has long been used as the original source of many traditional Chinese medicines (TCM) prescriptions for its pharmacological effects. Currently, this species is at risk of extinction owing to overexploitation. Genomic data can provide a scientific basis for the effective protection of wild germplasm resources.
